html:
The Tunguska event was a huge explosion over the forest of central Siberia on the morning of 30 June 1908, near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River in the Russian Empire. It is the largest impact event in recorded history.

A space rock, probably a small asteroid or a piece of a comet, blew up in the air several kilometres above the ground. It left no crater. The blast flattened some 80 million trees over more than 2,000 square kilometres, in a pattern pointing away from the centre. People 60 kilometres away were knocked off their feet and felt the heat, windows broke up to 200 kilometres away, and the night sky over Europe glowed for days.

The area was so remote, home to a few Evenki reindeer herders, that very few people died. No scientist went there until Leonid Kulik led an expedition in 1927. Tunguska is now the standard example of what an air burst can do.
